title: adaptive-saturation-throttle-and-kernel-fallback-for-cross-tenant-ttft-regression
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported sudden TTFT spikes and a sustained drop in tokens/sec for long-context model families after last week's kernel selector change. Root cause appears to be a combo of per-tenant request burst patterns + an aggressive kernel scheduling heuristic that moved some request classes to a kernel variant with worse KV cache locality for long prefixes. This ticket coordinates an emergency mitigation, a short-term hotpatch, and the longer-term fixes to prevent recurrence.

Observed behavior:
- First-byte latency (TTFT) increased by 1.8-3x for several customers using >8k token windows.
- Sustained tokens/sec dropped by ~30% under real traffic shapes (microbursts followed by slow tails).
- Issue reproducible on Hosted and Dedicated pools; Private customers reported similar symptoms after rolling runtime-1.20.

Immediate mitigation already applied:
- Tenant-level adaptive throttling rule deployed to limit concurrent high-prefix requests for impacted customers (rolled 2026-03-12 22:40 UTC).
- Emergency kernel heuristic rollback for two affected instance types (g5x16/g5x32) to the previous selector that favors KV locality (rolled 2026-03-13 01:10 UTC).
- Temporary increase to per-tenant token quota timeout to reduce queue buildup in front of the runtime.

Current status and next steps (this ticket):
1) Ship targeted hotpatch: introduce an adaptive saturation throttle inside the serving proxy that detects cross-tenant contention patterns and applies a fairness window (work: implement throttle + unit tests).
2) Extend kernel selector tests: add regression harness that simulates long-prefix KV cache miss patterns and measures tokens/sec across kernels (work: add to CI perf-suite).
3) Deploy refined kernel fallback policy: only fall back to alternate kernel when measured per-request cache locality meets threshold; additive safety checks to avoid throughput regressions.
4) Monitoring & alerting: create a dedicated Grafana dashboard with per-tenant TTFT/tokens/sec baselines + an automated detection rule (alert -> PagerDuty if deviation > 40% for 5m).
5) Customer comms & postmortem: coordinate customer notes, timelines, and a cross-functional RCA after stabilization.

Acceptance criteria:
- Measurable reduction in TTFT spikes for impacted tenants under replayed traffic (target: <20% regression vs baseline).
- Tokens/sec recovered to within 10% of pre-regression baseline for long-context workloads.
- New CI perf test catches this class of kernel-scheduling regression before merge.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Adaptive throttling reduces latency variance but can temporarily reduce throughput for noisy tenants; mitigation is to tune fairness window and allow burst tokens for low-latency SLAs.
- Kernel selector conservatism may miss some micro-optimizations; long-term plan is telemetry-driven heuristics rather than hard-coded rules.
